guides.title: Browser Timers in Background Tabs, Locked Phones, and Closed Tabs
guides.primaryQuestion: Will a browser timer keep working in a background tab, on a locked phone, or after I close the tab?
guides.author: Suhas Sunder

implementationEvidence.claim: Elapsed and remaining values are reconciled from monotonic performance readings rather than callback counts.
The shared elapsed stopwatch reconciles immediately when a running page becomes visible.

testEvidence: Recorded Chromium three-second countdown reconciliation check
verifiedClaims: The production countdown computes remaining time from a target performance timestamp.
The shared elapsed-stopwatch hook reconciles when the page becomes visible.
Closing the page removes the JavaScript execution context used by these tools.
qualifiedClaims: Hidden-page throttling, freezing, discard, device lock, and wake behavior vary by browser and operating system.
The recorded Chromium tab test did not simulate a physically locked mobile device.
claimsExcluded: Guaranteed alarm delivery while a device sleeps
Continued execution after the tab or browser is closed
Identical lifecycle behavior in Chromium, Firefox, and Safari
manualTests: Ran a three-second countdown, opened a second tab, waited 4.3 seconds, and observed 0:00 with the Finished state.
browserTests: Ran a three-second countdown, opened a second tab, waited 4.3 seconds, and observed 0:00 with the Finished state.
remainingLimitations: Hidden-page throttling, freezing, discard, device lock, and wake behavior vary by browser and operating system.
The recorded Chromium tab test did not simulate a physically locked mobile device.

guides.title: Why a Browser Timer or Alarm May Stay Silent
guides.primaryQuestion: Why did my browser timer finish without making a sound?
guides.author: Suhas Sunder

implementationEvidence.claim: Alarm audio creates or reuses Web Audio contexts and requests resume when suspended; the metronome schedules ahead on AudioContext.currentTime.

testEvidence: Recorded Chromium Online Alarm Clock Test sound interaction
verifiedClaims: The alarm creates or reuses a Web Audio context and requests resume when it is suspended.
The metronome schedules tones from AudioContext.currentTime.
A user can run the alarm sound test before relying on a scheduled cue.
qualifiedClaims: Audibility also depends on autoplay policy, volume, mute or silent mode, output routing, background policy, and device sleep.
Automation confirmed control execution and an empty warning/error log, not sound heard by a person.
claimsExcluded: Bypassing browser or operating-system audio policy
manualTests: Clicked Test sound from a user gesture in Chromium and observed no browser warning or error logs.
browserTests: Clicked Test sound from a user gesture in Chromium and observed no browser warning or error logs.
remainingLimitations: Audibility also depends on autoplay policy, volume, mute or silent mode, output routing, background policy, and device sleep.
Automation confirmed control execution and an empty warning/error log, not sound heard by a person.

guides.title: How Browser Timers Measure Elapsed Time and Handle Delays
guides.primaryQuestion: How can a browser timer stay accurate when animation frames and timer callbacks are delayed?
guides.author: Suhas Sunder

implementationEvidence.claim: Elapsed and remaining values are reconciled from monotonic performance readings rather than callback counts.
The shared elapsed stopwatch reconciles immediately when a running page becomes visible.
Alarm audio creates or reuses Web Audio contexts and requests resume when suspended; the metronome schedules ahead on AudioContext.currentTime.

verifiedClaims: Countdown and stopwatch paths reconcile from a target or elapsed reference instead of counting callbacks.
Reaction timing uses a monotonic performance reading.
Metronome scheduling uses the audio context clock while live clock displays derive from wall-clock time.
qualifiedClaims: Different tool families use different timing references and cannot share one universal precision claim.
Displayed milliseconds remain subject to input, rendering, display, browser, and device latency.
claimsExcluded: Universal drift correction across every route
Immunity to system-clock changes for wall-clock tools
manualTests: Observed the production countdown reach the expected target after a delayed inspection interval.
browserTests: Observed the production countdown reach the expected target after a delayed inspection interval.
remainingLimitations: Different tool families use different timing references and cannot share one universal precision claim.
Displayed milliseconds remain subject to input, rendering, display, browser, and device latency.

guides.title: Unix Timestamps in Seconds, Milliseconds, and Microseconds
guides.primaryQuestion: Is this Unix timestamp in seconds, milliseconds, or microseconds?
guides.author: Suhas Sunder

implementationEvidence.claim: Auto mode uses explicit digit thresholds, normalizes seconds and microseconds to milliseconds, and truncates sub-millisecond Date input.

testEvidence: Recorded Chromium Unix unit auto-detection checks
verifiedClaims: Auto mode treats 0 to 11 integer digits as seconds, 12 to 14 as milliseconds, and 15 or more as microseconds.
The converter normalizes seconds and microseconds to milliseconds for Date and truncates sub-millisecond input.
Equivalent example inputs in all three units resolve to the same UTC instant.
qualifiedClaims: Digit-count detection is a convenience heuristic and explicit units remain safer for unusual ranges.
Readable local output applies the viewer's timezone after the timestamp instant is resolved.
claimsExcluded: A Unix timestamp contains a timezone
Arbitrary-precision microsecond preservation in JavaScript Date
Support beyond the browser Date range
manualTests: Entered 1700000000, 1700000000000, and 1700000000000000 in auto mode; each resolved to 2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z with the expected unit label.
browserTests: Entered 1700000000, 1700000000000, and 1700000000000000 in auto mode; each resolved to 2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z with the expected unit label.
remainingLimitations: Digit-count detection is a convenience heuristic and explicit units remain safer for unusual ranges.
Readable local output applies the viewer's timezone after the timestamp instant is resolved.

guides.title: Daylight-Saving Gaps, Repeated Times, and Timezone Conversions
guides.primaryQuestion: Why can a local time be nonexistent or occur twice during a timezone conversion?
guides.author: Suhas Sunder

implementationEvidence.claim: The resolver finds zero, one, or multiple exact IANA-zone wall-time matches and sorts repeated-time matches chronologically.

testEvidence: Recorded Chromium DST gap and repeated-time checks
verifiedClaims: The production resolver classifies a wall time as nonexistent, valid, or ambiguous by matching IANA-zone parts.
America/New_York 2026-11-01 01:30 is labeled ambiguous and resolves to the earlier occurrence, 2026-11-01T05:30:00.000Z.
qualifiedClaims: Results depend on timezone rules available in the browser and operating system.
Historical rules and future political changes can differ from a fixed offset assumption.
claimsExcluded: A fixed offset is equivalent to a named timezone
The browser owns an independently updated authoritative timezone service
manualTests: Verified the documented 2026 New York spring gap and fall repeat in the production converter using deterministic URL inputs.
browserTests: Verified the documented 2026 New York spring gap and fall repeat in the production converter using deterministic URL inputs.
remainingLimitations: Results depend on timezone rules available in the browser and operating system.
Historical rules and future political changes can differ from a fixed offset assumption.

guides.title: What iLoveTimers Stores in Your Browser
guides.primaryQuestion: What does iLoveTimers save in my browser, and what is not saved?
guides.author: Suhas Sunder

implementationEvidence.claim: Theme and route-local persistence fall back safely when storage is missing, invalid, or unavailable.

testEvidence: Recorded Chromium speedcubing persistence and session-loss check
externalServices: PostHog can receive consented, path-only analytics when configured; user-entered tool values are not intentionally captured.
verifiedClaims: The evidence inventory records eleven production storage categories and their exact keys.
Speedcubing preferences persist in localStorage while solve results remain page-session memory.
Theme and route-local readers catch unavailable or corrupt storage and fall back safely.
qualifiedClaims: Private browsing, storage partitioning, browser policy, storage pressure, and user clearing can change persistence behavior.
Locally stored data is not a cloud backup or account record.
claimsExcluded: All browser profiles retain localStorage indefinitely
Stored values are synchronized across devices
No external service ever receives site usage data after consent
manualTests: Set Speedcubing Timer to Instant toggle with a 12-solve limit, recorded a result, reloaded, and confirmed preferences persisted while the result cleared.
browserTests: Set Speedcubing Timer to Instant toggle with a 12-solve limit, recorded a result, reloaded, and confirmed preferences persisted while the result cleared.
remainingLimitations: Private browsing, storage partitioning, browser policy, storage pressure, and user clearing can change persistence behavior.
Locally stored data is not a cloud backup or account record.

browserValidation.environment: Codex Desktop 26.715.7063 on Windows using the in-app Chromium browser against the local React Router production build at 127.0.0.1:3030; the automation API did not expose the exact Chromium runtime version. Desktop viewports were 1440x1000 and 1365x900; the mobile viewport was 390x844.
scenarios: Rendered the guides index, all six guide articles, and all eleven contextually linked tool routes in desktop light, desktop dark, mobile light, and mobile dark modes: 72 screenshots, 72 single-H1 checks, and zero document-level horizontal-overflow failures.
Verified all three guide tables remain inside horizontal-scroll wrappers at 390px rather than widening the document.

Rendered all 132 canonical non-redirect routes in Chromium: 132 paths matched, 132 single-H1 checks passed, canonical link metadata was present on every route, and no document-level horizontal overflow or hydration-error text was found.

Ran a three-second countdown, opened a second browser tab, waited 4.3 seconds, and confirmed the countdown reconciled to 0:00 with the Finished state. The automation environment continued to report the countdown page as visible, so this does not simulate operating-system freezing or a physically locked device.
Activated the Online Alarm Clock Test sound control from a user-gesture click and observed no browser warning or error logs.
Changed Speedcubing Timer preferences to Instant toggle and 12 maximum session solves, recorded a solve, reloaded, and confirmed the preferences persisted while the session result cleared.

Entered America/New_York 2026-03-08 02:30 and confirmed the converter rejected the nonexistent spring-forward time; entered 2026-11-01 01:30 and confirmed the earlier-occurrence ambiguity warning plus 2026-11-01T05:30:00.000Z.
Entered 1700000000 seconds, 1700000000000 milliseconds, and 1700000000000000 microseconds in auto-detect mode; all three resolved to 2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z with the expected unit labels.
Collected warning and error logs after the representative interaction tests and the 132-route sweep; no warnings or errors were reported.
screenshots: Guide and changed-tool matrix: 18 routes x desktop/mobile x light/dark = 72 captured viewport screenshots.
Representative visual inspection: guides index in desktop light and dark.
Representative visual inspection: browser-storage guide in desktop dark and 390px mobile light.
Representative visual inspection: Unix-units guide in 390px mobile dark and DST guide in desktop light.

limitations: The automation environment cannot reproduce physical device lock, operating-system sleep, browser process discard, or every background-throttling policy.
The sound control executed without console errors, but automation cannot confirm that a human heard audio through the machine's speakers.
The automation API did not expose the exact Chromium runtime version; the host Codex Desktop build is recorded instead.
This pass used the in-app Chromium browser; Firefox, Safari, mobile browser shells, and assistive-technology combinations were not independently exercised.
Corrupt or inaccessible localStorage fallback is covered by source review and automated safeguards rather than by mutating browser storage during this visual pass.

claimBoundaries: Browser tests cover Chromium on the recorded Windows environment, not every browser or mobile operating system.
Audible output is not machine-verified; the test records control response and console state, while a person must confirm what speakers produce.
No guide claims guaranteed background execution, official time synchronization, certified precision, or durable cloud storage.
